title: Transfers — a qualifying Metro/Glider transfer is charged £0.00
preface: This test is to confirm that a qualifying Metro/Ulsterbus-to-Glider transfer (or vice versa) is charged £0.00 rather than a normal fare, per the Glider transfer logic (CR123).
preconds:
**GIVEN** the seeded ABT test card makes two consecutive taps within the configured transfer time (e.g. 90 minutes) — a Directional feeder tap that is charged, then a Glider tap in the same direction whose TransferRouteType flag is not "None"
**AND** example: an Inbound tap on Ulsterbus feeder route G10D, followed by an Inbound tap on Glider East within the transfer window (FBD-100651 §7.4, Scenario 1 "Dir Fdr to GL")
**AND** you are signed in to the ABT Operator Portal to verify the card's Journey History

steps.content:
**WHEN** the two taps are matched as a transfer and the EndOfDay settlement runs
**AND** you open the card's Journey History
steps.expected:
**THEN** the first (feeder) tap is charged its normal fare
**AND** the second (Glider) tap is charged £0.00 and shown with the transfer icon
**AND** the transfer tap is sent to MERIT under the transfer product, not the standard ABT product

expected:
A qualifying Metro/Glider transfer tap is charged £0.00 and recorded as a transfer, while the originating tap is charged normally.

Data variations: Non-Directional feeder → Glider (FBD-100651 Scenario 3); Glider → feeder (Scenarios 2/4); Ulsterbus (transfers enabled) → Glider (Scenario 11). All require matching within the configured transfer time and, for a Directional flag, the same RouteDirection on both taps.

[Automatable: Yes · Cross-check: CloudFare / MERIT]
citations: FBD-100651 §7.4 para 300 (Glider Transfers overview — free transfer to/from Metro/Ulsterbus)

FBD-100651 §7.4.4-7.4.5 para 338-341 (Non-Directional on either tap, or matching RouteDirection on both, marks the new tap as a transfer)

change_note: RESOLVED gap: replaced the invented 'transfer capping rule' / 'Transfer Caps tab' premise (no such concept exists in the capping specs) with the real, spec-grounded Glider transfer behaviour — a qualifying transfer is charged £0.00 (FBD-100651, CR123), not capped. Retitled from a config-action case to an observable-behaviour case per the Gherkin standard; grounded with a concrete worked example (Scenario 1, G10D In → Glider East In) from the Glider Transfer Scenarios tracker. No existing case in suite 30279 covers this specific CR123 mechanism (the only other free-transfer case, C4103587, covers the separate bus-to-rail CR133/CR064 mechanism), so this is a reword, not a dedupe/condemn.
